page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the cost-optimized e2 family. It is equipped with 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical Intel Xeon core on the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in a fractional allocation of half of a physical core. The instance features 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local SSD storage or dedicated GPU hardware. The underlying processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz and features 16 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AES, and FMA instruction sets, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX capabilities.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the e2-medium is designed for light, non-intensive workloads. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is moderate, scoring 2642.19, but multi-core performance drops to a weaker tier at 2642.78 due to the shared-core resource limits. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 6.36 GB/sec and write speeds at 4.83 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect these limitations, yielding a single-core score of 661.0 and a multi-core score of 682.0. Database and web serving capabilities are also modest, with Redis SET operations reaching 0.82 million operations per second and static web serving throughput limited to 0.63 GB/sec.

This instance offers a highly cost-efficient profile for workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance compute resources. Because it utilizes shared physical hardware, it provides a low-cost entry point for development environments, small-scale testing, and lightweight background utilities. The primary tradeoff is the potential for resource contention and lower overall throughput compared to dedicated-core instances. It is best suited for basic web serving, microservices, lightweight application testing, and simple automation scripts.
